title: Iceland Ring Road in 10 Days: Snæfellsnes, Mývatn, the East Fjords, Jökulsárlón and the South Coast

tagline: Fire and ice all the way round: volcanoes, waterfalls, glaciers and black beaches
facts: Keflavík 1, Snæfellsnes 1, Akureyri 1, Vopnafjörður 1, East Fjords 1, Höfn area 1, Kirkjubæjarklaustur area 1, South Coast 1, Reykjavík 1
intro: A full circle of Iceland on the Ring Road. The Reykjanes peninsula, Snæfellsnes ('Iceland in miniature'), Akureyri in the north, the waterfalls and lava formations of Lake Mývatn, the quiet East Fjords, a zodiac among the icebergs of Jökulsárlón, Skaftafell under Europe's largest glacier, the black beaches and waterfalls of the south coast, and the Golden Circle back to Reykjavík. Our original plan hiked to the 2021 lava field near Grindavík; that area has been restricted since the 2023 to 2025 eruptions, so day 2 now explores the rest of the peninsula instead. Day 3 is a long drive, about 6 hours with stops.
highlights: The bridge between two continents on Reykjanes
Kirkjufell, Arnarstapi and the Snæfellsjökull volcano
Goðafoss, Dettifoss and the lava city of Dimmuborgir
The Hverfjall crater and the boiling mud of Námafjall

faqs.a: Yes, from June to August. Indian licence holders need an International Driving Permit, and gravel and wind insurance is strongly advised.

faqs.q: Will we see the northern lights?
faqs.a: Not in summer: it does not get dark. Travel from late September to March for the lights.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

faqs.q: Is there support while we travel?
faqs.a: Yes. You have our 24/7 travel desk on +91 97148 59797 and +91 98242 21400 and a WhatsApp group with your consultant for the whole trip.

good_to_know.title: Hotel deposit
good_to_know.text: Use a credit card for the deposit or pre-authorisation at check-in, never a forex or debit card. Forex cards cannot hold funds, many hotels refuse them, and a credit-card hold is released faster.

good_to_know.title: Cards and cash
good_to_know.text: On card machines, always choose to pay in Icelandic krónur (ISK), never in INR. Iceland is almost cashless; cards work even at remote fuel pumps (a PIN is needed).

good_to_know.title: Pickpockets
good_to_know.text: Busy stations, trams and squares are pickpocket hotspots. Keep passports in the hotel safe, carry a copy, and wear your bag in front in crowds.

good_to_know.title: Plugs, water and meal times
good_to_know.text: Plugs are the two round-pin type C and F at 230 volts (Switzerland uses type J; a type C plug fits). Tap water is safe to drink. Lunch is about 12:00 to 14:00 and dinner from about 18:30.

good_to_know.title: Reynisfjara and the beaches
good_to_know.text: Sneaker waves at Reynisfjara and other south-coast beaches have swept visitors away. Stay well back from the water's edge and never turn your back to the sea.

good_to_know.title: Volcanic areas
good_to_know.text: Eruptions on the Reykjanes peninsula since 2021 have closed roads and areas around Grindavík. Follow safetravel.is and your guide's instructions.

good_to_know.title: Weather
good_to_know.text: Wind and rain change by the hour. Waterproof jacket and trousers, layers and walking boots, even in summer.

dining_intro: Reykjavík and Akureyri have vegetarian and Indian restaurants; in the countryside choice is small, and lunch is often soup and bread at a farm café. We send your diet to every guesthouse in advance.
dining_avoid: Soups, sauces, risottos and even some vegetable dishes are often made with meat or fish stock, and many cheeses use animal rennet. Show the food card and ask before ordering.
food_card: We are strict vegetarians (Jain). No meat, fish, seafood or eggs. No onion, garlic, potato, carrot or any root vegetables. No meat or fish stock. Thank you.
